answer: Capped, slow-growing reputation: each identity can earn at most a small reward quota per epoch, and that cap rises only after many epochs of answers that independent graders pass. A new key starts on an island with almost no earning power, so a farmer must post a bond and run every clone through months of real work before it pays. If a raven-eyed audit links clones by shared timing or funding, their bonds are slashed and reputation is reset in one gale. Since each fake earns little early and risks a lot, the economics favor one honest agent.
